meta.profile: mid-maturity Australian bank (composite, fictional) — CyberArk-style vault deployed on the core estate, JIT/ZSP and cloud entitlement governance still maturing
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic illustrative posture authored to demonstrate the reporting pipeline. Does not represent any real institution or assessment.

UC-P-001.rationale: CyberArk vault holds Windows/AD privileged accounts but Unix/Linux and network-device passwords are onboarded inconsistently and several batch service accounts are still rotated by hand.

UC-P-002.rationale: Privileged sessions to in-scope servers route through the PAM proxy with credential injection and direct admin paths are blocked at the network layer.

UC-P-003.rationale: Sessions are recorded with searchable command metadata and retained per policy; high-risk command flagging is enabled though review SLAs are still being tuned.

UC-P-004.rationale: Most privileged roles still carry always-on standing membership; JIT elevation is piloted only for a handful of cloud admin groups, so zero-standing-privilege coverage is minimal.

UC-P-005.rationale: Scheduled discovery runs across AD and the major Unix estate but cloud, DB and SaaS local-admin accounts are scanned ad hoc and newly found accounts are onboarded manually.

UC-P-006.rationale: Application-to-application credentials are still largely hard-coded in config and CI variables; only two strategic platforms fetch credentials from the broker at runtime.

UC-P-007.rationale: MFA is enforced at the PAM elevation point for all in-scope access, but phishing-resistant FIDO2 is rolled out to only part of the tier-0 administrator population.

UC-P-008.rationale: Break-glass accounts are sealed, alert-on-use, require dual control at checkout and auto-rotate after use with an auto-raised incident for review.

UC-P-009.rationale: Standing local-admin has been removed from the standard SOE fleet but a sizeable population of developer and engineering workstations still retains local-admin pending an EPM rollout.

UC-P-010.rationale: Privileged entitlements are not yet right-sized against actual usage; no periodic least-privilege baseline review exists and excess grants accumulate over time.

UC-P-011.rationale: Strategic vendors connect through the recorded PAM proxy with JIT grants, but a few legacy support arrangements still rely on standing VPN and shared admin credentials.

UC-P-012.rationale: There is no continuous cloud entitlement analysis across AWS/Azure/GCP; over-permissioned cloud identities are only found during periodic manual reviews.

UC-P-013.rationale: Secretless privileged workload attestation has not yet been assessed; the platform team has flagged it for a future spike alongside the workload-identity program.

UC-P-014.rationale: Privileged accounts are recertified annually as part of the broader access review, but the cadence is not risk-tiered and a meaningful share of items are bulk-approved.

UC-P-015.rationale: Privileged session and credential-use telemetry is forwarded to the SIEM but no behavioural analytics or anomaly detection is applied to it today.

UC-P-016.rationale: The SOC has detections for pass-the-hash and Kerberoasting via the EDR/SIEM, but DCSync and token-theft coverage against privileged accounts is incomplete and not fully correlated.

UC-P-017.rationale: The PAM platform meets its availability and recovery targets with tested break-glass paths; cross-region failover is exercised though the full DR drill cadence is still being formalised.
